caption:
Pain just below the kneecap every time you jump, squat or take the stairs? Toto's new season doubled his training, and his knee noticed.

That's often patellar tendinopathy, also called jumper's knee. It usually shows up when jumping load climbs faster than the tendon can adapt.

Rest tends to calm it, but it often returns once you're back on court. What usually helps more is adjusting training and rebuilding tendon capacity gradually: holds, then slow strength work, then jumping and landing. Pain up to about 3–4 out of 10 that settles by the next morning is usually OK.

A pop, rapid swelling or the knee giving way are worth checking sooner. Our Chatswood physios can build your plan. Book online via the link in bio 🏀
